subject: prog-cont
title: PROG.CONT.------EXP.DY.
description: Diagram in EXT.F(II)-14, on the page where Braxton describes the migration of post-Ayler musicians to Paris and back, the cross-continental cycle that solidified post-Ayler creativity as a transition-grade thrust. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) is crossed with EXP-DYM (expansion dynamics). The diagram contains both (P)CULT-SOLD (the point of activation of culture solidification) and (C)AFL (the concept of affiliation) and (R)TM (the reality of terminology) — three explicitly prefixed nodes, marking that culture solidification, affiliation, and terminology are operating at distinct prefix-levels. EXP-DYM → PROG-CONT (the crossing); SOC-RT (social reality) → PROG-CONT; PRI-INFO (primary information) → PROG-CONT. PRI-INFO also → (P)CULT-SOLD → (C)AFL → (R)TM. PHY-U-P (physical universe particular) → PROG-CONT (a fourth feed). COS-D (cosmic dictates) → TRS (transition) → (R)TM, and COS-D → T-C-IMP (time continuum implications). Structural argument: progressional continuance is over-determined by *four* upstream feeds (expansion dynamics, social reality, primary information, physical universe particular) — meaning the seventies seven-fold cross-continental migration produced an unusually robust progressional continuance because all four upstreams were active. Real terminology is the convergence point — fed by both (c)affiliation (which is fed by the point-of-activation of culture solidification, which is fed by primary information) *and* by transition (which is fed by cosmic dictates). The diagram thus diagrams the seventies' opportunity: real terminology — Braxton's term for the *naming* of the music — could only become accurate when both the culture-solidification-via-affiliation chain *and* the cosmic-dictates-via-transition chain converged at it.
